taxonomy:
Below is a taxonomy built only from the rule texts you provided. I group the games by the primary action the solver performs on the grid, and then by the main structural logic the rules mention.

## 1. Placement / shading puzzles
These ask you to place objects, blacken cells, or choose white/black status.

### 1.1 Light-placement
- **Akari**  
  Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells constrain adjacent bulbs; bulbs illuminate orthogonally; all white cells must be lit; bulbs cannot light each other.

### 1.2 Binary black/white cell shading
- **Chained Block**  
  Fill cells black/white so black connected components are blocks with size clues; every block contains one clue or “?”; corner-touching blocks form chains; no chain may repeat a block size-and-shape up to rotation/reflection.
- **Choco Banana**  
  Paint some cells black; black connected cells must form rectangles/squares; white connected cells must not form rectangles/squares; numbers give area size.
- **Heyawake**  
  Fill cells, with painted cells counted by room clues; painted cells cannot touch orthogonally; white cells must stay connected; white runs cannot span more than two rooms in a straight line.
- **Hitori**  
  Color cells black so no number repeats in any row/column among white cells; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; white cells must be connected.
- **Kurodoko**  
  Color cells black; numbered cells stay white; numbers count visible white cells up/down/left/right to first black cell or edge; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; white cells connected.
- **Kurotto**  
  Color cells black; circled clue gives sum of lengths of orthogonally extending black runs from that circle; circle cells cannot be colored.
- **LITS**  
  Shade tetrominoes, one per room; same tetromino shape may not touch across rooms, even rotated/reflected; shaded cells connected; no 2×2 shaded square.
- **Norinori**  
  Place black cells in dominoes of size 2; each room contains exactly two black squares.
- **Nurimeizu**  
  Paint whole rooms black or leave whole rooms white; unpaintable symbol rooms stay white; white cells form a maze from S to G; circles must lie on shortest path, triangles must not; no 2×2 monochrome block; white cells connected and acyclic.
- **Nurimisaki**  
  Fill cells black/white; circled cells stay white and must be “promontories” with exactly one white orthogonal neighbor; circle numbers give white run length from that cell; white connected; neither color may form a 2×2 block.
- **Nurikabe**  
  Fill cells black/white; numbered cells stay white; each white island has exactly one number and size equal to it; black cells form one connected wall; no 2×2 black block.
- **Nuritwin**  
  Shade cells so each room contains exactly two shaded blocks of equal size; optional number gives size of one block; the two same-room blocks cannot touch orthogonally; all shaded cells globally connected; no 2×2 all-shaded block.
- **Sto-stone**  
  Fill designated cells black; room clues give count of connected black cells within that room; black cells may not connect across room borders before “dropping”; after dropping downward, stones must fill bottom half without gaps.
- **Tilepaint**  
  Color whole tiles black or white; diagonal-cell clues count black cells to the right or downward until boundary/another clue cell; final picture forms an object outline.
- **Usowan**  
  Fill cells black/white; numbered cells cannot be colored; each number gives adjacent black count, except exactly one wrong clue per room; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; white cells connected.
- **Yajilin**  
  Blacken some non-number cells; arrow clues count black cells in indicated direction; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; loop runs through remaining non-black, non-number cells.

### 1.3 Triangle placement / partial-cell covering
- **Shakashaka**  
  Place right triangles in cells (except black clue cells); remaining white regions must form rectangles/squares; clues count adjacent triangles.

### 1.4 Symbol / mark placement in cells
- **Juosan**  
  Fill each cell with either — or |; room clues compare counts of the two marks; horizontal marks may extend long horizontally but at most 2 vertically; vertical marks analogously.
- **Evolomino**  
  Place squares in some white cells; connected placed squares form blocks; each block contains exactly one square on a pre-drawn arrow; along an arrow, successive blocks increase by one square without rotation/reflection.

### 1.5 Number-sequence placement in cells
- **Hebi**  
  Place numbers 1 to 5 in snake cells so each snake is a connected sequence 1→2→3→4→5; snakes cannot touch orthogonally; directional visibility restriction from each snake’s head side; black arrow clues indicate nearest visible snake number or 0.

---

## 2. Region division / partition puzzles
These require drawing borders or otherwise partitioning the grid into regions/blocks.

### 2.1 Partition into arbitrary regions with size/adjacency rules
- **Five Cells**  
  Divide grid into blocks of exactly five cells; clues tell how many block edges surround a cell, counting outer frame.
- **Shikaku**  
  Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its area.
- **Sashigane**  
  Divide grid into one-cell-wide L-shaped blocks; open circles are knees and may give block size; arrow cells are ends pointing toward the knee.
- **Double Choco**  
  Draw borders over dotted lines to form blocks; each block contains a white area and gray area of the same shape/size up to rotation/reflection; number gives count of cells of that color, i.e. half the block size.

### 2.2 Partition implied by number-filled regions
- **Fillomino**  
  Fill all cells with numbers; orthogonally connected equal numbers form blocks; block size equals its number; equal-sized blocks may not touch orthogonally.
- **Makaro**  
  Fill rooms with numbers 1 up to room size; arrow clues indicate the largest adjacent number lies in the pointed cell; same numbers in different rooms may not touch orthogonally.
- **Ripple Effect**  
  Fill rooms with consecutive numbers starting at 1; equal numbers in a row/column must be separated by at least their value.
- **Sudoku**  
  Fill cells 1–9 so each row, column, and 3×3 box contains 1–9.
- **Nansuke**  
  Fill blank cells with numbers from a given list; entries read horizontally or vertically; one digit per cell.

---

## 3. Path and loop puzzles
These ask for drawing one or more continuous lines through the grid or between points.

### 3.1 Single loop through cell centers
- **Dotchi-Loop**  
  Draw one loop through cell centers; must include all white-circle cells and exclude black-circle cells; within each bold area, all white circles are all straight or all turning.
- **Masyu**  
  Draw one loop through all black/white circles; white circles are straight with a turn adjacent; black circles are turns with straight continuation on both sides.
- **Mid-loop**  
  Draw one loop through cell centers; each black circle is the midpoint of a straight segment of the loop.
- **Moon-or-Sun**  
  Draw one loop; each room is entered only once; in each room the loop visits all moons or all suns, not both; room types alternate moon/sun between consecutive visited rooms.
- **Nagareru**  
  Draw one directed single loop; must pass through black-arrow cells in arrow direction; black-cell arrows create wind affecting allowed movement and forced bending.
- **Suraromu**  
  Draw one loop through all “gates”; start/end at open circle; open-circle number gives number of gates to traverse; black-cell numbers indicate the order in which a gate is crossed.
- **Yajilin**  
  Draw one loop through non-black, non-number cells, together with black-cell placement constraints.

### 3.2 Single loop on lattice edges
- **Slitherlink**  
  Connect dots into one loop; cell numbers count surrounding edges used.

### 3.3 Multiple pair-connecting paths
- **Numberlink**  
  Connect equal numbers with non-crossing, non-branching paths through cell centers; numbered cells are endpoints and not traversed through.

### 3.4 Network connection between nodes
- **Hashiwokakero**  
  Connect numbered islands with 1 or 2 bridges; bridges are straight, non-crossing; each island’s degree equals its number; all islands connected.

### 3.5 Object plus outgoing path
- **Pencils**  
  Mark straight pencil bodies with a tip at one end; numbers inside a pencil give pencil length; line from tip travels through cells for as many cells as the pencil number; lines do not branch or self-cross.

---

## 4. Movement / relocation puzzles
These involve moving tokens from one place to another.

### 4.1 Move tokens to satisfy region occupancy
- **Satogaeri**  
  Move circles orthogonally so each country ends with exactly one circle; numbered circles move exactly that many cells, empty circles any distance or not at all; paths cannot cross or pass over circles.
- **Yosenabe**  
  Move circles orthogonally into gray areas, shown by straight arrows ending in gray cells; arrows cannot bend or cross circles/arrows; gray-area numbers equal sum of entering circle numbers; each gray area gets at least one circle.

---

## 5. Shape-formation and geometric-constraint puzzles
These are especially about shapes formed by connected cells.

### 5.1 Construct specified polyforms / shape growth
- **Evolomino**  
  Successive blocks along an arrow grow by exactly one square, preserving orientation and reflection state.
- **LITS**  
  One tetromino per room; identical tetromino shapes cannot touch across rooms.

### 5.2 Rectangle / square recognition constraints
- **Choco Banana**  
  Black components must be rectangles/squares; white components must not be.
- **Shakashaka**  
  Remaining white uncovered areas must be rectangles/squares.
- **Shikaku**  
  Final partition regions are rectangles.
- **Five Cells**  
  Not specifically geometric in final shape, but border-count clues constrain region geometry.
- **Sashigane**  
  Final regions are one-cell-wide L-shapes.

### 5.3 Same-shape matching within regions
- **Double Choco**  
  White and gray subareas in a block must match by size and shape up to rotation/reflection.
- **Nuritwin**  
  Each room contains two shaded blocks of equal size.
- **Chained Block**  
  Within each chain, no two blocks may share same size and shape up to rotation/reflection.

---

## 6. Visibility / line-of-sight clue puzzles
These use sightlines along rows/columns.

- **Akari**  
  Bulbs illuminate along rows/columns until black cell/frame.
- **Kurodoko**  
  Numbers count visible white cells until a black cell/frame.
- **Hebi**  
  Black arrow cells report nearest snake number in arrow direction; snakes also have forward line-of-sight attack restrictions.
- **Tilepaint**  
  Diagonal clues count black cells to the right or downward until stopping condition.
- **Yajilin**  
  Arrow clues count black cells in one direction.
- **Nurimisaki**  
  Circle numbers count white cells in a straight line from the promontory.
- **Kurotto**  
  Circle numbers sum orthogonally extending black runs.

---

## 7. Room-based puzzles
These explicitly rely on bold-bordered rooms as a key structure.

- **Dotchi-Loop**
- **Double Choco**
- **Heyawake**
- **Juosan**
- **LITS**
- **Moon-or-Sun**
- **Nurimeizu**
- **Nuritwin**
- **Ripple Effect**
- **Sashigane**
- **Satogaeri** uses “Countries”
- **Sto-stone**
- **Tilepaint**
- **Usowan**
- **Makaro**

Common room functions seen in the rules:
- room clue gives count: **Heyawake, Sto-stone**
- one object per room: **LITS** (one tetromino), **Norinori** (two black cells), **Satogaeri** (one circle after moving)
- all-or-nothing room coloring: **Nurimeizu, Tilepaint**
- room-local symbol choice: **Moon-or-Sun, Juosan**
- room-local number set: **Makaro, Ripple Effect**
- room-local paired structures: **Double Choco, Nuritwin**

---

## 8. Number-filling puzzles
The primary act is entering numbers into cells.

### 8.1 Latin / permutation style
- **Sudoku**  
  Row, column, and 3×3 box each contain 1–9.
- **Makaro**  
  Each room contains 1 to room size once each; cross-room adjacency restriction on equal numbers.

### 8.2 Region-size equals number
- **Fillomino**  
  Equal-number regions have size equal to their number.

### 8.3 Distance-sensitive number placement
- **Ripple Effect**  
  Equal numbers in row/column must be spaced by at least their value.

### 8.4 Number placement from external list
- **Nansuke**  
  Insert numbers from a provided list into across/down slots.

### 8.5 Sequential local patterns
- **Hebi**  
  Place numbers 1–5 in each snake.
- **Evolomino**  
  Not a number-filling puzzle, but has ordered growth structure rather than digit placement.

---

## 9. Connectivity-driven puzzles
A cross-cutting category: the main challenge is maintaining one connected structure.

### 9.1 Connected white region
- **Heyawake**
- **Hitori**
- **Kurodoko**
- **Nurimisaki**

### 9.2 Connected black region
- **Nurikabe**  
  Black wall connected.
- **LITS**  
  Shaded cells connected.
- **Nuritwin**  
  All shaded cells connected.

### 9.3 Connected graph / network
- **Hashiwokakero**  
  All islands connected by bridges.

### 9.4 Single-loop connectivity
- **Dotchi-Loop**
- **Masyu**
- **Mid-loop**
- **Moon-or-Sun**
- **Nagareru**
- **Slitherlink**
- **Suraromu**
- **Yajilin**

---

## 10. Compact taxonomy by primary mechanic
If you want a one-line classification for each title:

- **Akari** — light placement / visibility
- **Chained Block** — black/white shading with polyomino-chain uniqueness
- **Choco Banana** — shading with rectangle-vs-nonrectangle area constraints
- **Dotchi-Loop** — single loop through cells with room-based circle behavior
- **Double Choco** — region partition with matched white/gray shapes
- **Evolomino** — square placement with arrow-guided shape growth
- **Five Cells** — partition into size-5 regions
- **Fillomino** — number filling by region size
- **Hashiwokakero** — bridge network
- **Hebi** — number-sequence placement with snake visibility constraints
- **Heyawake** — room-based black/white shading
- **Hitori** — duplicate-elimination shading
- **Juosan** — mark placement with territory balance and run constraints
- **Kurodoko** — visibility shading
- **Kurotto** — shading by summed black runs from circles
- **LITS** — room tetromino shading
- **Masyu** — loop with black/white pearl turn rules
- **Nagareru** — directed loop with wind constraints
- **Nansuke** — place listed numbers into slots
- **Norinori** — paired black-cell placement by room
- **Nurimeizu** — room shading to create a maze path
- **Nurimisaki** — promontory white-cell shading
- **Makaro** — room number filling with local maximum arrows
- **Mid-loop** — loop with midpoint clues
- **Moon-or-Sun** — room-alternating symbol loop
- **Numberlink** — connect matching pairs
- **Nurikabe** — island-and-wall shading
- **Nuritwin** — twin shaded blocks in each room
- **Pencils** — pencil-shape marking with tip paths
- **Ripple Effect** — room number filling with distance rule
- **Sashigane** — partition into L-shaped regions
- **Satogaeri** — move circles among countries
- **Shakashaka** — triangle placement making rectangular white areas
- **Shikaku** — partition into numbered rectangles
- **Slitherlink** — edge loop with perimeter counts
- **Sto-stone** — shading with gravity/drop test
- **Sudoku** — Latin-style number placement
- **Suraromu** — loop through ordered gates
- **Tilepaint** — whole-tile coloring with line-count clues
- **Usowan** — shading with one false clue per room
- **Yajilin** — hybrid loop + black-cell placement with arrow counts
- **Yosenabe** — move circles into gray areas with sum constraints

If you want, I can turn this into a **tree diagram**, a **table with columns like “grid action / clue type / connectivity / region use”**, or a **JSON taxonomy**.
